item.title: Ladder 10 · Conventus dē conventibus (the meeting about meetings) · Latin only
item.description: Latin only. A funny pyramid: Gaius calls a meeting to cut meetings. "I will speak briefly" (then an hour), ut + subjunctive requests that crack, nisi … loquerētur, iam domī essem, quoniam nēmō audit, ego quidem tacēbō, cum … fīnītus esset. Iulia's voice.

item.title: Ladder 8 · 50 new words + 30 hard ones · Latin only
item.description: Latin only. Road to 2,000, set 1: the next 50 Road words (induō, tunica, sūmō, piscis, mūrus, umbra, collum, iaceō, stēlla, scaena…) in 5 scenes (morning, kitchen, walk, a long night, evening), each word heard 6+ times, plus your 30 stickiest hell words (quoniam, ideō, quidem, quīdam, tamen, īdem, tālis…) in clear sentences. Closing story of the whole day, then a quick-fire list of all 80 words. Free voice (IPA, v as v).

item.title: Ladder 7 · Docē mē, ut discam: pyramid 3 · Latin only (× 2)
item.description: Latin only. Commands + 'so that…' on how to learn, listen, ask, agree and avoid mistakes: Docē mē, ut discam · Audī mē, ut intellegās · Rogā mē, ut cōgitem · Loquāmur, ut cōnsentiāmus · Prīmum cōgitā, nē errēs. Quotes: Errāre hūmānum est, Docendō discimus. Played twice. Free voice (IPA, v as v).

item.title: Ladder 6 · ut, nē, cum: pyramid 2 · Latin only (× 2)
item.description: Latin only. Subjunctive pyramid 2, new sentences: Dīc fīliō meō ut domum veniat · Domum eō, ut cum līberīs cēnem · Timeō nē pīca mē oppugnet · Cum fessus essem, domī mānsī · Scīsne ubi sit cāseus? Slow steps, plain vs subjunctive contrasts, reviews (and pyramid 1's peaks), a funny rainy day at the end. Played twice. Free voice (IPA, v as v).

item.title: Ladder 5 · ut, nē, cum: the subjunctive pyramid · Latin only
item.description: Latin only. Slow steps, plain vs subjunctive contrasts, reviews, and a funny day at the end. English then Latin, free voice (IPA, v as v).

item.title: Chat · Fābulae · Latin only × 3
item.description: Latin stories about the family: a son who won't sleep, a wet dog, the cheese Marcus always forgets, and two daughters who find out they're in the stories. Easy stories or hard ones: which are better? Then Christmas and the Nativity. Quotes: Sinite parvulōs venīre ad mē (Mark 10:14), Glōria in altissimīs Deō (Luke 2:14). Latin only. The whole dialogue 3 times.
